learning_outcomes.text: Analyze, reason, and develop individually and in teams, different solutions for assemblies and subsystems of automotive and industrial vehicles that satisfy certain needs or objective functions.

Simulate the longitudinal, transverse, and vertical dynamic behavior of an automotive and industrial vehicle under various driver actions and external forces at the tire-road contact and aerodynamic forces.
Understand, analyze, and evaluate the results obtained in problem-solving and make decisions.
Apply programming knowledge to the simulation of vehicle dynamics and the calculation of vehicle subsystems.

syllabus_topics: General description of automobiles and industrial vehicles
Safety and control systems. Passive and active safety
Vertical, longitudinal, and transverse behavior of the tire
Power plant: engine. Torque and power curves
Typologies of traction systems. Advantages and disadvantages
Traction systems in electric and hybrid vehicles
Typologies and components of the braking system
Braking performance: distance, time, and braking efficiency
Components of the suspension system in automobiles
Components of the suspension system in industrial vehicles
Kingpin inclination angle or pivot angle
Directional response. Neutral, understeering, and oversteering vehicles
Decontamination and recycling. Directives. Current situation and forecasts
teaching_methods: Laboratory work (component identification, computational simulation using MATLAB)

assessment_methods.method: Tutored project or computational simulation work

assessment_rules: Students can choose between continuous or global assessment; continuous assessment is the default if no choice is made. For continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 4.5 in the written exam (AE1) is required for other activities to be averaged; otherwise, the final grade is the AE1 grade. The written exam (AE1) and the tutored project (AE3) are recoverable in the extraordinary call, while lab practices (AE2) are not, but their ordinary call grade is retained. Global assessment consists of an 80% written exam, 10% lab practice demonstration, and 10% demonstration of CAE simulation tools.
